title: Topological Sort
description:
Given a directed acyclic graph (DAG) with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, find a topological ordering of its vertices.

A topological ordering is a linear ordering of vertices such that for every directed edge $(u, v)$, vertex $u$ comes before vertex $v$.

If there are multiple valid orderings, print the lexicographically smallest one.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers $n$ and $m$ ($1 \leq n \leq 10^5$, $0 \leq m \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$) — the number of vertices and edges.

Each of the next $m$ lines contains two integers $u$ and $v$ ($1 \leq u, v \leq n$, $u \neq v$) — a directed edge from $u$ to $v$.

It is guaranteed that the graph is a DAG (no cycles) and contains no duplicate edges.
outputFormat: Print $n$ space-separated integers — the lexicographically smallest topological ordering of the vertices.
constraints:
$1 \leq n \leq 10^5$
$0 \leq m \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$
The graph is a DAG with no duplicate edges.
